annual_compliance: NGO Law (39/11): annual financial statements submitted to the registrar; those with income above EUR 10,000 publish the annual report on their website; neglect risks strike-off from the register.

Law on Associations and Foundations: the assembly adopts annual work and financial reports, published on the association's website and filed with the competent state body; neglect risks deregistration.
Law 80/2021: NPOs submit annual financial statements (balance sheet, income statement) to the competent authority by 31 March of the following year; neglect risks deregistration.
NCO Law (86/2020): annual activity report published within 6 months of year-end; no formal strike-off for late filing, but activity contrary to national security or public order grounds termination.

The annual activity-report duty under the Public Organisations Law (4572-VI) was abolished (Law 767-VII); no periodic registrar filing for typical NGOs, only standard legal-entity tax and financial reporting.

Each year by 1 March the association sends the registering authority its continued-activity information and the list of elected governing-body members; foundations also publish an annual property report.
Ordinance 26/2000: annual activity and financial reports to the competent administrative authority, published in the Official Gazette; late filing risks fines or deregistration.

Triple annual filing: activity report to Statistics (due ~31 May), financial statements to the NRA if income or expenses exceed 500 BGN, and an annual fee to the registration office; neglect risks deregistration.
Foundations (Law 4182/2013, art. 59) submit budget, final accounts and balance sheet to the competent authority yearly and an asset-usage plan every two years; non-compliance risks deregistration.

Societies notify the registrar annually on administrative matters; non-profit companies file annual returns and accounts within ~9-12 months of year-end, with late-filing penalties and deregistration risk.

Enrolled VOs submit Annual Returns (return, report, accounts) to the Commissioner for Voluntary Organisations after each financial year (S.L. 492.02); the register is public; non-compliance risks deregistration.

Charities Act 2009 s.52: Annual Report to the Charities Regulator within 10 months of year-end (31 October for December year-end); non-filing is an offence and the Regulator may strike the charity off.
Charities Act 2011: annual return and accounts to the Charity Commission within 10 months of the accounting reference date; accounts are public; persistent non-filing risks removal from the register.
Plain associations have no statutory annual filing to the register; entities within the Act on Annual Accounts file accounts by 31 August; the general meeting adopts the annual report and accounts.
Foundations file annual report and accounts with the Register of Company Accounts by 31 July; plain associations only if they have an accounting obligation; late filing incurs fees and supervision.

Most associations have no annual filing duty; larger ones (two of: assets EUR 7.5m, turnover EUR 15m, 50 employees) file financial statements with the PRH Register of Associations; non-filing risks fines.
Foundations file annual reports with Bolagsverket within 7.5 months of year-end (late-filing fees); simple associations have no statutory filing duty, accounts are adopted at the general meeting.

Voluntary associations (frivillige foreninger) have no statutory reporting duty to CVR, only re-confirmation of the CVR number every 3 years; annual accounts are prepared for members; inactivity risks deregistration.

Non-profit associations (MTU) submit annual financial statements (balance sheet, income statement) to the e-Business Register within 6 months of year-end (30 June for calendar year); non-filing risks removal.

Associations (biedribas) file annual reports with the Enterprise Register even without commercial activity (simplified records); after 2 years of non-filing the registrar may deregister; the register is public.
